made, its model also predicts the image the firmware leaves, command for
command; the two are compared byte for byte. The sweep's save takes a new
head, erases it and copies 17 live records (28 commands); the cut test
build stops after each command and part way through each page program
(109 cuts), and the model adds programs with half their bits cleared and
erases half done (29 images). Every image holds the old patch or the new
and nothing else changed, and the shipping image starts from each one,
finds what `tools/store.py` finds, and saves again. The busy test build
makes each erase take 12 ms and each page program 3 ms, the part's
longest (HW-77; an earlier run at 400 ms an erase passed too). Under
audioload's input (test patch 6 on all 16 voices, core 0 at 82 000
instructions a block on average), SAVE held three times makes the keys it
strikes meanwhile save to their slots: 24 saves, one of them erasing a
sector (18 ms), and still no underrun, the longest fill 419 us of a
1 451 us block, and every tick within 2 time base ticks. The screen's
event line after a save, a refused save and a reset is checked against
golden images.

#### Open (SR-9's open questions)
- **Q-21, the part:** read on a unit; the ID check above refuses to write
  to any other until its datasheet is read.
- **Q-22, SPI0 on the chip:** how the window's controller hands the flash
  to SPI0 and back, SPI0's clock and mode, and the chip select (fwtest
  takes PD0; on the chip it may be another pin). The driver writes only
  HW-47's bits; what the chip needs goes in `store_init` and the select
  functions. Core 1 already runs from RAM, so it needn't be stopped.
- **Q-23, write protection:** if a unit's protect bits are set, a write
  reads back wrong and the save is reported failed (never silently lost).
- **Q-24, updates:** whether an update rewrites the user region decides
  whether saved patches survive one (M9).
| R-MIDIOUT-6 | The round trip: midiout's golden MIDI out, played into MIDI in at the times it was sent (the script derived from the golden file, checked), plays the same notes: every byte parsed as the model does, the same note ons and offs, at the end the same patch, algorithm, mode and four knobs as midiout's panel left, and each note played alone within 0.05 semitones of midiout's pitch. | M6b | C-FW-SUITE, C-UNIT |
| R-MIDIOUT-7 | The queue's policy when the wire can't keep up: 32 messages; a control change (but data entry, the parameter numbers and the mode messages), pitch bend, pressure or program change replaces a waiting one of the same kind, channel and controller when only such messages wait after it; 8 places are kept for note offs (and all notes off, all sound off); another message that finds the rest full is dropped and counted; a note off that finds the queue full drops the newest waiting message that ends no notes; a note on dropped has its note off dropped too. The burst test build (in one block: 16 note ons, 20 moves of one controller, 10 bends, 16 more note ons, 32 note offs): the controllers and bends merge, note ons past the room are dropped with their offs, no note off is lost, every note on the wire ends, the wire's timing holds (R-MIDIOUT-1), and the panel's keys afterwards go out within the latency bound (golden files). | M6b | C-FW-SUITE |

sub('docs/STORE-FORMAT.md',"""Chip offsets `0xEA000` to `0xFBFFF`, the stock layout's user patch
region (HW-80): 18 sectors of 4 KiB, used as a ring.""","""Chip offsets `0xFC000` to `0xFEFFF`, the stock layout's unused region
(HW-80): 3 sectors of 4 KiB, used as a ring. The firmware leaves the
stock firmware's user patch region (`0xEA000` to `0xFBFFF`, where M7's
store was) as it is, so the stock firmware's saved patches survive; why
three sectors are enough is in docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md (M8a). The format
does not depend on the number of sectors.""")
s=open('docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md').read()
s+="""
### 2026-10-25 M8a: the store moves to the unused region

The owner prefers that our firmware never erases the stock firmware's
saved patches. M7's store took the stock user patch region (HW-80,
`0xEA000` to `0xFBFFF`, 18 sectors), so it erased them. HW-80 names one
other region a store may take without touching anything of the stock
firmware's: `0xFC000` to `0xFEFFF`, 12 KiB, three sectors, ending before
the per-unit last 4 KiB. The store now lives there (`STORE_BASE`,
`STORE_SIZE`; the format is unchanged), and the image is still linked to
end before `0xEA000`, so neither touches the user patch region. No unit
runs a build with M7's store yet, so nothing is migrated.

**Does it fit?** Everything the store keeps live at once is 16 patches
(a record of 128 bytes each), the selection (32), the settings (64) and
a reset (16): 2 160 bytes. A sector holds 4 080 bytes of records after
its header. The ring moves the live records of the sector after the new
head into it, so a sector is never erased with anything live in it; even
when every live record has to move, the new head keeps 1 920 bytes for
new records, more than the largest record (128). So no save is ever
refused for want of room, with any mix of slots in use; the model and
the store suite's `full` and `wear` cases run on three sectors.

**Wear life.** Each sector takes 100 000 erases (HW-77), 300 000 for the
region. Counted with `tools/store.py`'s model, with all 16 slots, the
selection and the settings live (the worst case, since every live record
must be copied round the ring):

| Use, without a break | Writes per erase | Life, 3 sectors | (M7's 18 sectors) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| the selection and the settings both changed every 2 s (the most `STORE_SETTLE_S` allows) | 31.6 pairs | 0.60 years (5 300 hours) | 4.7 years |
| a patch saved every 10 s | 30.9 saves | 2.9 years | 17.6 years |

Each erase takes about 3 000 to 4 000 bytes of new records. A heavy
day's real use, 300 program changes, 20 settings changes and 20 saves,
is about 13 KiB of records, four or five erases a day: about 180 years.
Two hours a day of the most writing the limits allow (both changed every
2 s for two hours) still lasts about 7 years. So the smaller region meets
the 16 slots, the selection and the settings with a long life; the cost
is the margin for abuse (an hour of non-stop changes wears 1/5 300 of the
region instead of 1/41 000). If that ever matters, `STORE_SETTLE_S` is the
lever: at 10 s the worst case lasts five times longer.

**Tests.** The constants test checks the store lies past the user patch
region and before the last 4 KiB, and the image's window ends where the
user patch region begins. The store suite's `persist` and `wear` cases
start with the user patch region full of a pseudo-random pattern standing
for the stock firmware's saved patches, and every run checks the chip
outside the store is unchanged, so an erase or a write there would fail.
"""
open('docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md','w').write(s)
EOF

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# The firmware's fwtest suite (docs/HARNESS.md, "Suites"). tools/fw-suite.py
# puts the image under test at out/fw/app.bin and the test images (the same
# source built with one SB_TEST_* define each) beside it, runs this suite
# through tools/fwtest, and then checks the captures: its docstring says how.
#
# boot (R-BOOT-1, R-BOOT-4, R-BOOT-5, R-CLK-1, R-IRQ-1, R-IRQ-2): main runs,
#   writes the marker and the console line, measures the clock and starts
#   the tick; RAM from 0x01c7fc00 to the vector table is as fwtest started
#   it (the r0 block, then zeros): golden files, exact. The beacon and the
#   vector table are checked by tools/fw-suite.py (the table against the
#   ELF's symbols, so a code change doesn't need a new golden file).
# heartbeat, heartbeat2 (R-BOOT-2, R-BOOT-3, R-BOOT-4, R-IRQ-1, R-IRQ-2):
#   1.25 and 2.25 s on the tick, the beacon captured along the way; the
#   watchdog fails the run if the beat count stops for 5 ms. The two differ
#   only in length, so their difference is the steady state (since M2).
# screen (R-LCD-1 to R-LCD-4): the address pattern at 300 ms, the test
#   screen at 800 ms and, one heartbeat later, at 1 500 ms: golden images,
#   exact, and tools/fw-suite.py checks every pixel of the pattern and the
#   test screen's border, corners and ramps on its own.
# flood (R-LCD-5): a test build sends whole frames back to back once the
#   test screen is up; every tick must keep its timing.
# fault (R-IRQ-4): a test build overruns main's stack; the next tick finds
#   the guard overwritten, reports it on the console and halts.
# stray (R-IRQ-3): a test build raises an interrupt nothing handles; its
#   stub reports the source on the console and halts.
# badinsn (a limit of the harness, no requirement): an undecodable
#   instruction ends the run with fwtest's own fault, before any handler of
#   ours could run (SR-1).
# Since M3, the panel's controls and LEDs (scripts in tests/fw/scripts/;
# the input record at 0x01c00060 holds the events, tools/fw-suite.py
# checks them and compares them with tests/fw/events/<case>.txt):
# keys (R-KEY-1, R-KEY-2, R-LED-1, R-LED-3, R-INPUT-1): every key and
#   button alone: the right control, debounce latency, its LED lit while
#   held and no other.
# chords (R-KEY-2, R-KEY-3, R-ENC-1, R-INPUT-2, R-LCD-6): chords, a
#   would-be ghost, keys held in the encoders' columns, chatter, a glitch;
#   the panel screen against a golden image (since M5 at 1 050 ms, one
#   frame after the last change it shows, not 1 030: the panel is drawn
#   in frames).
# encoders (R-ENC-1, R-ENC-2, R-INPUT-3): slow, fast, shared columns, all
#   seven at once with a chord and a pot sweep; every tick still on time.
# pot (R-POT-1, R-POT-2): steps, the ends, noise at rest, a sweep.
# leds (R-LED-2): a test build sets each LED to its own brightness.
# ledshow (R-LED-3): the keys script on a test build whose scan times when
#   it first drives an LED main has just set.
# Since M4, audio (--wav, --ipb; the audio record at 0x01c00550; our own
# analysis, tools/audio_analysis.py):
# tone (R-AUD-1, R-AUD-4): the test tone's frequency, level and THD+N, a
#   clean start and stop, and silence at rest around it.
# notes (R-AUD-2, R-AUD-5, R-AUD-6): single notes' pitch, level (MASTER),
#   latency from the key and from its event, no clicks, silence between.
# audioload (R-AUD-1, R-AUD-3, R-INPUT-3, R-FM-6): 10.9 s of the heaviest
#   input (since M5 the FM engine's: test patch 6 on all 16 voices, 20 keys
#   struck again in turn, six encoders, MASTER, the tone): no underrun,
#   every tick on time, both cores rendering.
# audiogold (R-AUD-7): a note and the tone, the whole output against a
#   golden WAV, exact. It moves whenever startup or the scan's timing
#   moves a note by a block (later milestones will): run the suite, check
#   that every other audio case passes, then copy audiogold/audio.wav
#   over golden/audiogold/audio.wav in the same commit.
# underrun (R-AUD-3): a test build late for one block in 64: each counted
#   and reported on the console, and the output goes on.
# Since M5, the FM engine (scripts fm*.txt; the engine's record at
# 0x01c00590; tools/fw-suite.py's checks, the test patches' values from
# tools/fm_patch.py). The notes case plays its test patch 0 since M5.
# fmbessel (R-FM-1): test patch 1's sidebands against Bessel functions.
# fmenv (R-FM-3): test patch 2's envelope stages, rates and levels.
# fmmono (R-FM-5): mono, legato and glide on test patch 3.
# fmsteal (R-FM-4): 17 notes held on 16 voices, one stolen, no click.
# fmvel (R-FM-3): a test build whose keys play five velocities.
# fmgold, fmgold2 (R-FM-8, R-FM-9): every test patch against a golden WAV,
#   twice: the same bytes both times. Regenerate it as audiogold's.
#

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

#
# The firmware's fwtest suite (docs/HARNESS.md, "Suites"). tools/fw-suite.py
# puts the image under test at out/fw/app.bin and the test images (the same
# source built with one SB_TEST_* define each) beside it, runs this suite
# through tools/fwtest, and then checks the captures: its docstring says how.
#
# boot (R-BOOT-1, R-BOOT-4, R-BOOT-5, R-CLK-1, R-IRQ-1, R-IRQ-2): main runs,
#   writes the marker and the console line, measures the clock and starts
#   the tick; RAM from 0x01c7fc00 to the vector table is as fwtest started
#   it (the r0 block, then zeros): golden files, exact. The beacon and the
#   vector table are checked by tools/fw-suite.py (the table against the
#   ELF's symbols, so a code change doesn't need a new golden file).
# heartbeat, heartbeat2 (R-BOOT-2, R-BOOT-3, R-BOOT-4, R-IRQ-1, R-IRQ-2):
#   1.25 and 2.25 s on the tick, the beacon captured along the way; the
#   watchdog fails the run if the beat count stops for 5 ms. The two differ
#   only in length, so their difference is the steady state (since M2).
# screen (R-LCD-1 to R-LCD-4): the address pattern at 300 ms, the test
#   screen at 800 ms and, one heartbeat later, at 1 500 ms: golden images,
#   exact, and tools/fw-suite.py checks every pixel of the pattern and the
#   test screen's border, corners and ramps on its own.
# flood (R-LCD-5): a test build sends whole frames back to back once the
#   test screen is up; every tick must keep its timing.
# fault (R-IRQ-4): a test build overruns main's stack; the next tick finds
#   the guard overwritten, reports it on the console and halts.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Measures the firmware's size, RAM and speed, and gates them (checks
C-PERF and C-PERF-PROBES; R-PERF-1 to R-PERF-5).
  perf.py check --build DIR --out DIR [--base-ref REF] [--records-ref REF]
                [--require-records]
      Measures DIR/app.bin (a tools/build.sh output), finds the latest
      record of a main commit (the first-parent history of --base-ref,
      default origin/main, on --records-ref, default origin/records),
      measures that record's own app.bin the same way, and applies the
      gates. Writes OUT/perf.json. Exit status 1 if a gate failed.
  perf.py probes --build DIR --out DIR
      Builds the firmware with SB_PROBE_SLOW, SB_PROBE_BIG and (since
      M4b) SB_PROBE_LOADED (firmware/src/probe.c), measures each, and
      checks that the gates fail each one for its own reason, measured
      against DIR/app.bin: the slower build its speed and its steady-state
      budget, the bigger build each size budget and its startup budget,
      the loaded build its loaded speed and loaded budget, with the
      unmodified build's measurements as those budgets. Builds it also with SB_PROBE_STACK
      and checks the stack's high-water mark shows at least the 1 KiB that
      build is known to use.
      Exit status 1 if any gate did not fail as it should.
  perf.py history --record REPORT.json --csv FILE [--measures FILE]
      Appends the record's line to perf-history.csv (records workflow),
      and since M4b its rows to perf-measures.csv, one per measure. Never
      rewrites either file; a commit (and measure) that already has a
      line is left.
  perf.py summary --record REPORT.json
      Prints the record's performance as Markdown (for the CI summary).
What is measured (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M0e):
- size: code, data, bss, the raw image and the stack reserved, from
  app.size; static RAM is data + bss (since M7 + ram_code, the code run
  from RAM);
- the stack's high-water mark: the firmware fills its unused stack with
  STACK_FILL once at startup (crt0.S, sb_stack_fill), so the deepest the
  stack went is the lowest word no longer holding it, in the stack
  captured at the end of the run. An image without the fill (an older
  record's) is read by the lowest non-zero word, as fwtest starts RAM at
  zero; that method can't see words written as zero;
- speed (since M2, the owner's decision): emulated core-0 instructions,
  in two parts, from two runs that differ only in length (RUN_MS):
  - steady state, per period: the longer run's instructions less the
    shorter's, divided by the periods gained between their ends. Since M4
    the period is the audio block (64 stereo frames, 1.451 ms), counted by
    fwtest itself as the rows of `ipb.csv` (`--ipb`, which changes no
    count); an image without audio output (one from before M4) has none,
    so its measurement says so and the speed gate doesn't compare with
    it. Until M4 the period was the heartbeat (one beat per millisecond,
    the beats the beacon gained). Both runs end a quarter of a second
    past a whole second, so the window between them holds whole seconds and none of
    the firmware's work timed on whole seconds or tenths of a second
    falls near its ends (an end can come up to about 30 ms late while the
    image idles, docs/HARNESS.md "Time");
  - startup: the instructions of the shorter run beyond its periods at the
    steady-state rate, the one-off work before the firmware settles.
  The stack's high-water mark is read at the end of the longer run.
  Until M2 speed was the instructions of one one-second run divided by
  its beats, startup included;
- loaded (since M4b, R-PERF-2): the same two runs again, with the fixed
  input script LOAD_SCRIPT, which drives the firmware to its heaviest
  steady load (every voice sounding, every control moving), and its
  steady state per period worked out the same way. Its budget
  (`loaded_per_period`) is optional: a milestone without one has the
  measure recorded and reported, not gated.
The gates: each budget in config/budgets.json for the current milestone
must hold: code, static RAM, stack high-water, startup instructions and
steady-state instructions per period. Steady-state instructions per period
may also rise by at most `speed_rise_percent` against the baseline, when
the baseline's record was made under the same steady-state budget;
otherwise that comparison is not made, and the record says why. Since M3
a record under the current budget that still holds the image of the last
record before that budget was raised (the raise's own merge, or any merge
after it that changed no firmware) is never the baseline: it is skipped,
and the baseline note names it (choose_baseline). A fall of
more than that is reported as an improvement. Startup has its budget but
no such comparison. The count is deterministic, so there is no noise

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Measures the firmware's size, RAM and speed, and gates them (checks
C-PERF and C-PERF-PROBES; R-PERF-1 to R-PERF-5).
  perf.py check --build DIR --out DIR [--base-ref REF] [--records-ref REF]
                [--require-records]
      Measures DIR/app.bin (a tools/build.sh output), finds the latest
      record of a main commit (the first-parent history of --base-ref,
      default origin/main, on --records-ref, default origin/records),
      measures that record's own app.bin the same way, and applies the
      gates. Writes OUT/perf.json. Exit status 1 if a gate failed.
  perf.py probes --build DIR --out DIR
      Builds the firmware with SB_PROBE_SLOW, SB_PROBE_BIG and (since
      M4b) SB_PROBE_LOADED (firmware/src/probe.c), measures each, and
      checks that the gates fail each one for its own reason, measured
      against DIR/app.bin: the slower build its speed and its steady-state
      budget, the bigger build each size budget and its startup budget,
      the loaded build its loaded speed and loaded budget, with the
      unmodified build's measurements as those budgets. Builds it also with SB_PROBE_STACK
      and checks the stack's high-water mark shows at least the 1 KiB that
      build is known to use.
      Exit status 1 if any gate did not fail as it should.
  perf.py history --record REPORT.json --csv FILE [--measures FILE]
      Appends the record's line to perf-history.csv (records workflow),
      and since M4b its rows to perf-measures.csv, one per measure. Never
      rewrites either file; a commit (and measure) that already has a
      line is left.
  perf.py summary --record REPORT.json
      Prints the record's performance as Markdown (for the CI summary).
What is measured (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M0e):
- size: code, data, bss, the raw image and the stack reserved, from
  app.size; static RAM is data + bss (since M7 + ram_code, the code run
  from RAM);
- the stack's high-water mark: the firmware fills its unused stack with
  STACK_FILL once at startup (crt0.S, sb_stack_fill), so the deepest the
  stack went is the lowest word no longer holding it, in the stack
  captured at the end of the run. An image without the fill (an older
  record's) is read by the lowest non-zero word, as fwtest starts RAM at
  zero; that method can't see words written as zero;
- speed (since M2, the owner's decision): emulated core-0 instructions,
  in two parts, from two runs that differ only in length (RUN_MS):
  - steady state, per period: the longer run's instructions less the
    shorter's, divided by the periods gained between their ends. Since M4
    the period is the audio block (64 stereo frames, 1.451 ms), counted by
    fwtest itself as the rows of `ipb.csv` (`--ipb`, which changes no
    count); an image without audio output (one from before M4) has none,
    so its measurement says so and the speed gate doesn't compare with
    it. Until M4 the period was the heartbeat (one beat per millisecond,
    the beats the beacon gained). Both runs end a quarter of a second
    past a whole second, so the window between them holds whole seconds and none of
    the firmware's work timed on whole seconds or tenths of a second
    falls near its ends (an end can come up to about 30 ms late while the
    image idles, docs/HARNESS.md "Time");
  - startup: the instructions of the shorter run beyond its periods at the
    steady-state rate, the one-off work before the firmware settles.
  The stack's high-water mark is read at the end of the longer run.
  Until M2 speed was the instructions of one one-second run divided by
  its beats, startup included;
- loaded (since M4b, R-PERF-2): the same two runs again, with the fixed
  input script LOAD_SCRIPT, which drives the firmware to its heaviest
  steady load (every voice sounding, every control moving), and its
  steady state per period worked out the same way. Its budget
  (`loaded_per_period`) is optional: a milestone without one has the
  measure recorded and reported, not gated.
The gates: each budget in config/budgets.json for the current milestone
must hold: code, static RAM, stack high-water, startup instructions and
steady-state instructions per period. Steady-state instructions per period
may also rise by at most `speed_rise_percent` against the baseline, when
the baseline's record was made under the same steady-state budget;
otherwise that comparison is not made, and the record says why. Since M3
a record under the current budget that still holds the image of the last
record before that budget was raised (the raise's own merge, or any merge
after it that changed no firmware) is never the baseline: it is skipped,
and the baseline note names it (choose_baseline). A fall of
more than that is reported as an improvement. Startup has its budget but
no such comparison. The count is deterministic, so there is no noise

---
name: perf-gate-steady-state
description: "Owner's 2026-10-22 decision on how the speed gate treats milestone work (startup vs steady state budgets)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d0aa28c2-493e-48cb-b0fd-be2a2d41a714
  modified: 2026-10-22T23:27:49.932Z
---

Decided by the owner in session M2 (2026-10-22): perf measures startup cost and steady-state cost per period separately (two run lengths; steady = difference; record both). Both get per-milestone budgets in config/budgets.json, raised only by their own PR with the reason, like code and RAM. The +3% gate applies only to steady state, between records under the same budget; startup has a budget but no 3% gate. R-PERF-2 amended in its own PR, before the M2 budgets PR.

**Why:** a new milestone's one-off startup work (e.g. M2 drawing the screen) would otherwise fail the +3% gate by design.

**How to apply:** when a milestone adds startup work, raise the startup budget in the budgets PR; keep per-period work within +3% or raise the steady budget in its own PR with the reason.

**M3 rule (owner, 2026-10-23; replaces the first-record rule of #39):** a main record is a speed baseline only if its firmware image SHA-256 differs from the image of the last record before the current steady budget was raised; records still holding that pre-raise image are skipped and named in the baseline note (perf.py choose_baseline). Reason: an unrelated merge (#43) landed between the budgets PR and the firmware PR, and records can be written out of order.

**How to apply:** a milestone raising steady needs only: budgets PR, then firmware PR, in any interleaving with unrelated merges.

**M5 (2026-10-23):** the baseline is chosen per budget *value*. A budgets PR that lowers a budget (M5 loaded 131 072 → 98 304) fails CI until main's image fits it, so the PR that brings the improvement (#66, the screen) must merge first. Then the budgets PR's record holds that image and is skipped as a baseline, so the next firmware PR's new, heavier measure is gated by the budget alone. Order: improvement → budgets → firmware.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md'; s=open(p).read()
i=s.index('**Wear life.** Each sector takes 100 000 erases'); j=s.index('**Tests.** The constants test')
new='''**Wear life,** counted as M7 counts it (its "Wear", a bound): each
sector takes 100 000 erases (HW-77), and each erase gives at least the
1 920 bytes left after the largest compaction, so the region takes
3 x 1 920 x 100 000 bytes of records, a sixth of M7's 18 sectors:

| Use, without a break | Life, 3 sectors | (M7's 18 sectors, same bound) |
|---|---:|---:|
| the selection and the settings both changed every 2 s (the most `STORE_SETTLE_S` allows; 96 bytes in 2 s) | 0.38 years (3 300 hours) | 2.3 years |
| a patch saved every 10 s | 1.4 years | 8.6 years |
| a heavy day: 300 program changes, 20 settings changes, 20 saves (about 13 KiB of records) | about 117 years | |
| two hours a day of the most the limits allow | about 4.6 years | |

The bound is pessimistic: `tools/store.py`'s model, with all 16 slots,
the selection and the settings live, takes about 3 000 to 4 000 bytes of
new records an erase, not 1 920, so real lives are about 1.6 to 2 times
these. So the smaller region meets the 16 slots, the selection and the

A `gh run download` of a CI report artifact brings the whole record, including its `harness/` folder of harness test results. M7 (2026-10-24) did that twice, opened only named logs, deleted both and recorded it in EXPOSURE.md.

**Why:** the clean-room rules let clean sessions take only named files of the firmware's own records; a whole artifact is the record wholesale.

**How to apply:**
- Read CI results from `gh run view <id> --log` first.
- If an artifact file is needed, name the file, or delete the artifact at once and record it.
- C-SEP-TERMS gives only a place and a hash (`sha256(word)[:16]`). Hash the flagged line's words the same way to find the word.
- A false positive goes in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json` by its own PR, which keeps a budget PR clean.

Related: [[provenance-ids-race]]

Clean and spec sessions run at the same time and both append PROVENANCE rows. In M6a (2026-10-24) my P-39 to P-42 were taken by spec PRs #77, #81 and #82 before mine merged, and I had to renumber twice.

**Why:** an ID is taken by whichever PR merges first, and both sides append at the table's end, so every pair of such PRs also conflicts there.

**How to apply:** before numbering, read `PROVENANCE.md` on each open spec PR's branch through `gh api .../contents/PROVENANCE.md?ref=<branch>` (docs only, never a fetch of their branch), take the next free ID, and expect to merge main into the PR and keep both rows. Also run `tools/clean-update.sh` from main only: on a feature branch its fast-forward stops before its barrier checks. Related: [[perf-gate-steady-state]].

T=$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp && cat > $T/c3.txt <<'EOF'
firmware: the store moves to the unused region, 0xFC000 to 0xFEFFF

What:    STORE_BASE and STORE_SIZE now name the stock layout's unused
         region (three sectors, ending before the per-unit last 4 KiB)
         instead of the stock firmware's user patch region, which our
         firmware now never erases or writes; the image is still linked
         to end where that region begins. tools/store.py follows, the
         constants test checks both regions, and the store suite's
         persist and wear cases start with the user patch region full of
         a pattern that must survive every save, erase and compaction.
         STORE-FORMAT.md, R-STORE-1 and R-STORE-8 say so; DESIGN-NOTES.md
         (M8a) has the numbers. The four MIDI out goldens and midiround's
         script follow a start-up 16 us shorter.
Why:     M8a, step 1: the owner prefers that the stock firmware's saved
         patches survive (HW-80), if the unused region meets 16 user
         slots, the selection and the settings with a stated wear life.
How:     everything live at once is 2 160 bytes and a sector holds 4 080,
         so a ring of three never refuses a save. Wear, by M7's own
         bound: 3 x 1 920 x 100 000 bytes of records, a sixth of M7's;
         a heavy day (300 program changes, 20 settings changes, 20
         saves) lasts about 117 years, and the selection and settings
         changed every 2 s without a break 0.38 years; the model gives
         1.6 to 2 times those. The format is unchanged; no unit runs
         M7's store, so nothing is migrated. MIDI out: reading 3 sector
         headers instead of 18 starts the audio 16 us sooner, so every
         timestamp moved 0.015 to 0.016 ms, and one of midithru's thru
         messages a block, with every byte the same; the goldens were
         checked so and copied, and tools/midi_scripts.py rewrote
         midiround's script from them, as boot.suite says.
Result:  local run: C-UNIT, the build and C-PERF pass; C-FW-SUITE's store
         cases all pass (persist, sweep, reset, corrupt, full, wear,
         migrate, busy, wipe), its other cases but the four MIDI out
         goldens, which this commit updates.
Sources: P-56
Exposure: firmware side, none
EOF
cat $T/trailer.txt >> $T/c3.txt && git add -A firmware tools tests docs PROVENANCE.md && git status --short && git commit -q -F $T/c3.txt && git log --oneline -1; rm -rf out/record; df -h . | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}'

/*
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
 * SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
 *
 * The instrument's interface (M8a; docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M8a, and
 * docs/M8-PROPOSAL.md): one screen at a time, HOME back to the patch
 * view, the bottom strip naming what KNOB1 to KNOB4 do on every screen.
 *
 * - The engine owns the interface's state (struct fm_ui): it reads the
 *   panel's events in order in its block callback, so a screen button
 *   and a knob turned just after it are taken in that order, and what a
 *   knob does always matches the screen it was turned on. It adds one to
 *   fm_ui.seq on every change and wakes main.
 * - Main only draws (views.c): it reads the state when seq holds still,
 *   works out what each part of the screen should show, and redraws and
 *   sends only the parts that changed, in frames, within the drawing
 *   budget (panel.c's since M5). It also sets the LEDs (input_led is main
 *   context only): a held button or key fully lit, the screen's own
 *   button lit, the selected operator's key at half brightness.
 */

#ifndef UI_H
#define UI_H

#include "sb.h"

/* The screens, in fm_ui.screen. */
#define UI_PATCH     0u   /* HOME: the patch view */
#define UI_EDIT      1u   /* EDIT: operators and the algorithm */
#define UI_ENV       2u   /* ENV: an envelope */
#define UI_SETTINGS  3u   /* GLO: the settings */
#define UI_SCREENS   4u

/* The interface's state, written by the engine only (fm_play.c). */
struct fm_ui {
    u32 seq;      /* one more on every change */
    u8 screen;    /* UI_* */
    u8 op;        /* the selected operator, 0 to 5 */
    u8 page;      /* the screen's page (SELECT steps through them) */
    u8 row;       /* the settings' row */
    u8 env;       /* ENV: 0 the operator's envelope, 1 the pitch envelope, 2 glide */
    u8 confirm;   /* settings: 1 while the factory reset waits for SAVE */
    u8 knobs;     /* 0: KNOB1 to KNOB4 are the macros; 1: direct (midi_settings.knobs) */
    u8 reserved;
};
extern volatile struct fm_ui fm_ui;

/* What views.c needs of the engine (fm_play.c). */
const u8 *fm_program_bytes(void);   /* the program playing now, as patch bytes */
u32 fm_user_used(void);             /* user slots holding a patch, bit n for slot n */

/* views.c, from main's loop: take the panel's events (LEDs, the event
 * line) and the engine's state, and draw what changed. view_message puts
 * a message on the event line, with a number after it unless it is 0. */
void view_serve(void);
void view_message(const char *text, u32 number);

/* The interface's record, after the store's (firmware/app.ld), for the
 * tests (tools/fw-suite.py reads this layout). Times in time base ticks. */
#define UI_MARKER 0x38495553u   /* "SUI8" in memory order */
struct sb_ui_record {
    u32 marker;
    u32 screen;        /* the screen drawn last */
    u32 seq;           /* fm_ui.seq as drawn last */
    u32 shows;         /* whole screens drawn (the first, and each change of screen) */
    u32 frames;        /* frames begun */
    u32 items;         /* parts of the screen drawn and sent */
    u32 rows_sent;     /* rows sent to the panel */
    u32 item_max;      /* the longest single part, drawn and sent */
    u32 block_max;     /* the most drawing time spent in one audio block */
    u32 over;          /* blocks whose drawing went past the budget (by its last part) */
    u32 leds;          /* LED changes main made */
    u32 messages;      /* messages put on the event line */
    u32 live;          /* live updates drawn (since M8a's later parts) */
    u32 live_max;      /* the longest */
    u32 reserved[2];
};
extern volatile struct sb_ui_record sb_ui;

#endif

def build_tests(build):
    """Builds the test images; returns problems."""
    problems = []
    for name, define in sorted(TEST_BUILDS.items()):
        out = os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", "build-" + name)
        p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/build.sh", "build", "--out", out, "--define", define],
                           cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            problems.append("%s: the build failed:\n%s" % (name, p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")[-2000:]))
            continue
        shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(out, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", name + ".bin"))
        print("built %s (-D%s)" % (name, define))
    return problems


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--build", required=True, help="a tools/build.sh output folder")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="where the suite's outputs go (empty or new)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, os.path.dirname(IMAGE)), exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(a.build, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, IMAGE))
    global START_SLACK
    size = os.path.join(a.build, "app.size")
    if os.path.exists(size):
        with open(size) as f:
            sizes = dict(l.split() for l in f if l.strip())
        print("image size: " + ", ".join("%s %s" % kv for kv in sizes.items()))
        START_SLACK = start_slack(int(sizes.get("bss", 0)))
        print("start slack: %d time base ticks (bss cleared before main starts the time base)" % START_SLACK)
    symbols = elf_symbols(os.path.join(a.build, "app.elf"))
    problems = build_tests(a.build)

    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "suite", SUITE, "--out", out], cwd=ROOT,
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    print(p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip())
    if p.returncode != 0:
        problems.append("fwtest suite exited %d" % p.returncode)

    steady = {}
    for name in EXPECT:
        path = os.path.join(out, name, "result.json")
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            problems.append("%s: no result.json" % name)
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            result = json.load(f)
        problems += check_case(name, result)
        run = result.get("run", {})
        print("%s: %s at %s ms, %s instructions on core 0"
              % (name, run.get("outcome"), run.get("emulated_ms"),
                 run.get("instructions", {}).get("core0")))
        for g in result.get("golden") or []:
            print("  golden %s: %s" % (g.get("name"), g.get("result")))
            if g.get("result") != "match":
                problems.append("%s: golden %s: %s" % (name, g.get("name"), g.get("detail")))
        if name in ("boot", "screen", "fault", "stray", "chords") and not result.get("golden"):
            problems.append("%s: no golden files compared" % name)
        case_dir = os.path.join(out, name)
        more, lines = [], []
        if name == "boot":
            more, lines = check_boot(case_dir, symbols)
        elif name in ("heartbeat", "heartbeat2") and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_heartbeat(case_dir, result)
            with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
                steady[name] = (result, beacon(f.read()))
            if len(steady) == 2:
                m, l = check_steady([steady["heartbeat"][0], steady["heartbeat2"][0]],
                                    [steady["heartbeat"][1], steady["heartbeat2"][1]])
                more, lines = more + m, lines + l
        elif name == "screen":
            more, lines = check_screen(case_dir)
        elif name == "flood" and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_flood(case_dir, result, os.path.join(out, "screen"))
        elif name == "fault":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STACK, 1)
        elif name == "stray":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STRAY, 127)
        elif name in INPUT_CHECKS and run.get("outcome") == EXPECT[name]:
            more, lines = INPUT_CHECKS[name](case_dir)
        elif name in AUDIO_CHECKS and run.get("outcome") == EXPECT[name]:
            try:
                more, lines = AUDIO_CHECKS[name](case_dir)
            except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
                more, lines = ["%s: %s" % (name, e)], []
        problems += more
        if lines:
            print("\n".join(lines))

    # Since M7, the store's cases: chained runs (tools/store_suite.py).
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, IMAGE), "rb") as f:
        image_len = len(f.read())
    more, _ = store_suite.run(sys.modules[__name__], out, image_len)
    problems += more

    for prob in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + prob)
    print("fw suite: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def build_tests(build):
    """Builds the test images; returns problems."""
    problems = []
    for name, define in sorted(TEST_BUILDS.items()):
        out = os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", "build-" + name)
        p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/build.sh", "build", "--out", out, "--define", define],
                           cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            problems.append("%s: the build failed:\n%s" % (name, p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")[-2000:]))
            continue
        shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(out, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", name + ".bin"))
        print("built %s (-D%s)" % (name, define))
    return problems


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--build", required=True, help="a tools/build.sh output folder")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="where the suite's outputs go (empty or new)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, os.path.dirname(IMAGE)), exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(a.build, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, IMAGE))
    global START_SLACK
    size = os.path.join(a.build, "app.size")
    if os.path.exists(size):
        with open(size) as f:
            sizes = dict(l.split() for l in f if l.strip())
        print("image size: " + ", ".join("%s %s" % kv for kv in sizes.items()))
        START_SLACK = start_slack(int(sizes.get("bss", 0)))
        print("start slack: %d time base ticks (bss cleared before main starts the time base)" % START_SLACK)
    symbols = elf_symbols(os.path.join(a.build, "app.elf"))
    problems = build_tests(a.build)

    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "suite", SUITE, "--out", out], cwd=ROOT,
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    print(p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip())
    if p.returncode != 0:
        problems.append("fwtest suite exited %d" % p.returncode)

    steady = {}
    for name in EXPECT:
        path = os.path.join(out, name, "result.json")
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            problems.append("%s: no result.json" % name)
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            result = json.load(f)
        problems += check_case(name, result)
        run = result.get("run", {})
        print("%s: %s at %s ms, %s instructions on core 0"
              % (name, run.get("outcome"), run.get("emulated_ms"),
                 run.get("instructions", {}).get("core0")))
        for g in result.get("golden") or []:
            print("  golden %s: %s" % (g.get("name"), g.get("result")))
            if g.get("result") != "match":
                problems.append("%s: golden %s: %s" % (name, g.get("name"), g.get("detail")))
        if name in ("boot", "screen", "fault", "stray", "chords") and not result.get("golden"):
            problems.append("%s: no golden files compared" % name)
        case_dir = os.path.join(out, name)
        more, lines = [], []
        if name == "boot":
            more, lines = check_boot(case_dir, symbols)
        elif name in ("heartbeat", "heartbeat2") and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_heartbeat(case_dir, result)
            with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
                steady[name] = (result, beacon(f.read()))
            if len(steady) == 2:
                m, l = check_steady([steady["heartbeat"][0], steady["heartbeat2"][0]],
                                    [steady["heartbeat"][1], steady["heartbeat2"][1]])
                more, lines = more + m, lines + l
        elif name == "screen":
            more, lines = check_screen(case_dir)
        elif name == "flood" and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_flood(case_dir, result, os.path.join(out, "screen"))
        elif name == "fault":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STACK, 1)
        elif name == "stray":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STRAY, 127)
        elif name in INPUT_CHECKS and run.get("outcome") == EXPECT[name]:
            more, lines = INPUT_CHECKS[name](case_dir)
        elif name in AUDIO_CHECKS and run.get("outcome") == EXPECT[name]:
            try:
                more, lines = AUDIO_CHECKS[name](case_dir)
            except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
                more, lines = ["%s: %s" % (name, e)], []
        problems += more
        if lines:
            print("\n".join(lines))

    # Since M7, the store's cases: chained runs (tools/store_suite.py).
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, IMAGE), "rb") as f:
        image_len = len(f.read())
    more, _ = store_suite.run(sys.modules[__name__], out, image_len)
    problems += more

    for prob in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + prob)
    print("fw suite: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    """Every audio case: the output ran, each block was filled once, the
    console holds nothing but the start line (and the underruns expected),
    and the WAV is mono in stereo (left equals right). Returns (problems,
    lines, record, wav) where wav is (left, block ends) or None."""
    problems, lines = [], []
    a = audio_record(os.path.join(case_dir, audio_name()))
    ends = aa.read_ipb(os.path.join(case_dir, "ipb.csv"))
    if a["marker"] != AUDIO_MARKER:
        problems.append("%s: the audio record's marker is 0x%08x" % (name, a["marker"]))
    # The end capture can come while the last block's fill is still going.
    if not len(ends) - 1 <= a["blocks"] <= len(ends):
        problems.append("%s: %d blocks filled, fwtest finished %d" % (name, a["blocks"], len(ends)))
    if a["underruns"] != underruns:
        problems.append("%s: %d underruns, expected %d" % (name, a["underruns"], underruns))
    if a["dropped"]:
        problems.append("%s: the engine's queue dropped %d events" % (name, a["dropped"]))
    gaps = [i for i in range(1, len(ends)) if not 0 < ends[i] - ends[i - 1] < 2 * BLOCK_TICKS / TICKS_PER_MS]
    if gaps:
        problems.append("%s: blocks %s ended more than a block after the one before" % (name, gaps[:5]))
    with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "console.txt")) as f:
        console = f.read()
    if not console.startswith(HELLO):
        problems.append("%s: the console doesn't start with the start line" % name)
    lines.append("  audio: %d blocks filled (fwtest: %d), %d underruns, longest fill %.1f us, "
                 "%d events to the engine"
                 % (a["blocks"], len(ends), a["underruns"], a["fill_max"] / 24.0, a["taken"]))
    wav = None
    path = os.path.join(case_dir, "audio.wav")
    if os.path.exists(path):
        rate, left, right = aa.read_wav(path)
        if left != right:
            problems.append("%s: left and right differ" % name)
        if len(left) != aa.BLOCK * len(ends):
            problems.append("%s: %d samples for %d blocks" % (name, len(left), len(ends)))
        lines.append("  audio.wav: %d frames (header %d Hz; measured at %.3f Hz)" % (len(left), rate, aa.RATE))
        wav = (left, ends)
    return problems, lines, a, console, wav

# Requirements

Numbered requirements for this project (the original, MIT-licensed base
firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1, JieLi AC791N). Every check names the
requirements it covers (`tools/record.py`, `CHECKS`), and every test record
ends with a traceability table: requirement → checks → result.

A requirement whose "Checked by" says *review* is checked by people when they
review a pull request, not by a machine. *Planned* means a later milestone
adds the check. The record lists both kinds, so nothing looks checked when it
isn't.

The four founding requirements (docs/prompts/M0a.md): **history**,
**tests**, **reproducible**, **public and efficient**.

| ID | Requirement | Since | Checked by |
|----|-------------|-------|------------|
| R-PROC-1 | Every commit message follows `.gitmessage` (subject `<area>: <summary>`; non-empty What, Why, How, Result, Sources, Exposure). Agent-written commits also carry `Model:` and `Claude-Session:` trailers. Merge commits are exempt; their pull request carries the sections. | M0a | C-COMMIT-MSG, C-UNIT |
| R-PROC-2 | main changes only through pull requests that passed CI, merged by the owner with a verified, signed merge commit (GitHub's merge button since 2026-10-22, CONTRIBUTING.md "Merge policy"). Nobody bypasses. No force pushes or deletion on main and `records`; `m*` tags are never moved or deleted. | M0a | rulesets (CONTRIBUTING.md); C-MERGE (records workflow) |
| R-PROC-3 | Each milestone's prompt is committed unedited in `docs/prompts/` in the commit that starts the milestone. | M0a | review |
| R-PROC-4 | Every check names the requirements it checks, and every record has a traceability table. | M0a | C-UNIT |
| R-REC-1 | Each commit pushed to main gets a permanent record `records/<sha>/` (report.json, report.md, logs) on the orphan `records` branch, written only by the records workflow, never for pull requests. A record is never changed: a later re-check of C-MERGE alone, started by hand with the merge check on main (`.github/workflows/recheck-merge.yml`), only adds `records/<sha>/verified-<date>/` beside it, naming the checker's commit and why. | M0a | records.yml; C-UNIT (record writer) |
| R-REC-2 | Each record has an OpenTimestamps proof. Upgraded proofs are added as new files and never replace the originals. | M0a | records.yml, ots-upgrade.yml |
| R-REPRO-1 | The toolchain is downloaded and checked against the SHA-256 in docs/TOOLCHAIN.md. It is never committed or published. | M0a | C-IMAGE, C-NO-TOOLCHAIN |
| R-REPRO-2 | The build container's base image is pinned by digest, its packages come from a pinned snapshot.debian.org date, and builds run under `linux/amd64` through `tools/build.sh`. | M0a | C-IMAGE |

input.command:
cat >> docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md <<'EOF'

### 2026-10-25 M8a: the screens' framework

The instrument's interface (docs/M8-PROPOSAL.md, with the owner's
answers in docs/prompts/M8a.md), first its frame. `firmware/src/ui.h`
and `views.c`; M3's panel screen (`panel.c`) is gone.

- **Who owns what.** The engine owns the interface's state (`struct
  fm_ui`: the screen, the selected operator, the page, the settings
  row). It already takes the panel's events in order in its block
  callback, from its own queue; so a screen button and a knob turned just
  after it reach it in that order, and what a knob does always matches
  the screen it was turned on. Had main decided the screen, an EDIT
  press and a KNOB1 turn in one block could reach the engine as a macro
  turn. The engine adds one to `fm_ui.seq` on every block that took an
  event or a MIDI message, and wakes main. Main only draws: it copies the
  state when `seq` holds still, works out what each part of the screen
  should show, and redraws only the parts that changed.
- **The frame.** Every screen has a header (rows 0-25: the program's
  number, `001` to `009` for the test patches and `U01` to `U16` for the
  user slots, its name at double size, the mode and the octave), a body
  (rows 26-189, the screen's own), an event line (rows 190-201) and the
  bottom strip (rows 202-239), which names what KNOB1 to KNOB4 do on this
  screen, with their values at double size, in four columns of 60
  pixels. Until M8a's patch view lands, KNOB1 to KNOB4 keep M5's meanings
  on every screen, and the strip says so.
- **Parts, frames and the budget.** M5's rule stays: what is marked is
  drawn at most once a 16 ms frame, part by part, and no part starts in
  an audio block once drawing has taken 4 352 time base ticks of it. A
  whole new screen is many parts: the header; the body cleared in four
  bands; the body drawn into the frame buffer; the body sent in four
  bands; the event line; the strip. A knob turn redraws only the strip's
  values and sends their 16 rows. The first build drew a body as one part
  of 11 300 ticks; split so, the longest part is 3 800 ticks (the strip's
  names and values after a change of screen), within the budget, and a
  block's drawing is under two budgets. Two things made that: a fast path
  for double-size text (a glyph pixel is one 32-bit store of two
  pixels) and not padding the body's text, whose bands are cleared
  anyway. A body is marked once a change, since its parts may take
  several blocks: marking it again while they were under way restarted
  its clearing and never finished (found in the first run).
- **LEDs.** A held button or key is fully lit, the shown screen's button
  lit, and on EDIT and ENV the selected operator's key at half. Main
  sets them (`input_led` is main's only) as it takes each event, from
  the same events the engine takes, so they change within R-LED-3's
  1 ms, not a block later when the engine's state arrives.
- **The heartbeat** stays the test screen's: main no longer draws it
  once the instrument's screens show (it drew over their rows 200-215
  every second).
- **The record.** `sb_ui` at `0x01C00870`, after the store's: the screen
  drawn, the parts, rows sent, the longest part and which, the most
  drawing in one block, the LED changes and messages.
- **Costs.** Code 26 700 bytes (+2 560). The steady state (the test
  screen, no input) 1 872 instructions a block, as before; the loaded
  measure 98 265, down from 107 590, as the screens redraw less than the
  M3 panel did under the same input.
EOF

### 2026-10-25 M8a: the screens' framework

The instrument's interface (docs/M8-PROPOSAL.md, with the owner's
answers in docs/prompts/M8a.md), first its frame. `firmware/src/ui.h`
and `views.c`; M3's panel screen (`panel.c`) is gone.

- **Who owns what.** The engine owns the interface's state (`struct
  fm_ui`: the screen, the selected operator, the page, the settings
  row). It already takes the panel's events in order in its block
  callback, from its own queue; so a screen button and a knob turned just
  after it reach it in that order, and what a knob does always matches
  the screen it was turned on. Had main decided the screen, an EDIT
  press and a KNOB1 turn in one block could reach the engine as a macro
  turn. The engine adds one to `fm_ui.seq` on every block that took an
  event or a MIDI message, and wakes main. Main only draws: it copies the
  state when `seq` holds still, works out what each part of the screen
  should show, and redraws only the parts that changed.
- **The frame.** Every screen has a header (rows 0-25: the program's
  number, `001` to `009` for the test patches and `U01` to `U16` for the
  user slots, its name at double size, the mode and the octave), a body
  (rows 26-189, the screen's own), an event line (rows 190-201) and the
  bottom strip (rows 202-239), which names what KNOB1 to KNOB4 do on this
  screen, with their values at double size, in four columns of 60
  pixels. Until M8a's patch view lands, KNOB1 to KNOB4 keep M5's meanings
  on every screen, and the strip says so.
- **Parts, frames and the budget.** M5's rule stays: what is marked is
  drawn at most once a 16 ms frame, part by part, and no part starts in
  an audio block once drawing has taken 4 352 time base ticks of it. A
  whole new screen is many parts: the header; the body cleared in four
  bands; the body drawn into the frame buffer; the body sent in four
  bands; the event line; the strip. A knob turn redraws only the strip's
  values and sends their 16 rows. The first build drew a body as one part
  of 11 300 ticks; split so, the longest part is 3 800 ticks (the strip's
  names and values after a change of screen), within the budget, and a
  block's drawing is under two budgets. Two things made that: a fast path
  for double-size text (a glyph pixel is one 32-bit store of two
  pixels) and not padding the body's text, whose bands are cleared
  anyway. A body is marked once a change, since its parts may take
  several blocks: marking it again while they were under way restarted
  its clearing and never finished (found in the first run).
- **LEDs.** A held button or key is fully lit, the shown screen's button
  lit, and on EDIT and ENV the selected operator's key at half. Main
  sets them (`input_led` is main's only) as it takes each event, from
  the same events the engine takes, so they change within R-LED-3's
  1 ms, not a block later when the engine's state arrives.
- **The heartbeat** stays the test screen's: main no longer draws it
  once the instrument's screens show (it drew over their rows 200-215
  every second).
- **The record.** `sb_ui` at `0x01C00870`, after the store's: the screen
  drawn, the parts, rows sent, the longest part and which, the most
  drawing in one block, the LED changes and messages.
- **Costs.** Code 26 700 bytes (+2 560). The steady state (the test
  screen, no input) 1 872 instructions a block, as before; the loaded
  measure 98 265, down from 107 590, as the screens redraw less than the
  M3 panel did under the same input.
EOF

def parse(stream):
    p = Parser()
    for b in stream:

# The four knobs' controllers (M6a's map, firmware/src/fm_play.c): a
# controller's 64 is no offset, 0 and 127 the ends of each knob's span.
KNOB_SPAN = ((-24, 24), (-32, 32), (-64, 32), (-7, 7))


def _div(a, b):
    """C's integer division: toward zero."""
    q = abs(a) // abs(b)
    return q if (a >= 0) == (b > 0) else -q


def knob_offset(k, v):
    """The knob offset MIDI in takes from controller value v."""
    lo, hi = KNOB_SPAN[k]
    return _div((v - 64) * hi, 63) if v >= 64 else _div((64 - v) * lo, 64)


def knob_value(k, p):
    """MIDI out's inverse (M6b): the smallest controller value whose
    offset is the knob position p, held to the span. Written from the
    rule, not the C: searched, not computed."""
    lo, hi = KNOB_SPAN[k]
    p = max(lo, min(hi, p))
    cands = [v for v in range(128) if knob_offset(k, v) == p]
    return min(cands, key=lambda v: abs(v - 64))
